paper: step 8. Provisional Section 3.3. The commons reference evaluation model is a trained artifact.
adr: Training lives under tools/evaluator-training/. This file is the LoRA run: base, hyperparameters, framework pins, seed. The generation recipe is recipe.json. The held-out suite is not an input. The training base returns to Qwen3-0.6B. Size is not the lever: the 1.7B sweep landed within noise of the 0.6B sweep, which proved the bottleneck was corpus register narrowness, not model capacity. This run holds every hyperparameter at the earlier 0.6B values so the register-augmented corpus is the only variable across the two 0.6B sweeps. 0.6B is also the phone-deployment target. The live pin is unchanged.

base.note: Read at run time from the manifest. repoId here is a pin that must match. This is the training base, kept as its own manifest field so the live pin is never implicitly retrained. The live evaluator pin stays baseRepoId/fileName (Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 at v2.1) until a trained candidate passes the gate. Do not train Qwen3-0.6B-Base; that is the pretrained checkpoint, not the post-trained instruct one.

framework.whyNotUnsloth: 0.6B plus 4548 short examples does not need Unsloth's memory path. The standard stack is the one a reader can follow without a third training runtime.
framework.reportToNote: No cloud metric sink. Loss logs to stdout and artifacts/train-log.json. Trackio would be a Hub side channel this run does not need.
framework.torch: supplied by the GPU image; not pinned here so a CUDA wheel is not overwritten

train.gradientCheckpointingNote: Off, as in the earlier 0.6B sweep. A 0.6B LoRA at per-device batch 8 and sequence 4096 fits an 80GB card without recomputing activations. Checkpointing is numerically identical either way, so this setting is about speed and about matching the earlier run, not about results. Turn it on only if a larger base returns.
train.enableThinkingNote: Qwen3 thinking must stay off. Inference uses QwenChatWrapper thoughts=discourage. Training applies enable_thinking=False so the assistant target is the compact verdict line, with the stock empty think block as prefix outside the mask. Do not set assistant_only_loss to false.
train.chatTemplateNote: Stock Qwen3 template plus {% generation %} around assistant content. TRL assistant_only_loss needs those spans. Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B share this template. Rendered text must match stock; train.py refuses to start if it does not, or if the assistant mask is empty, or if no-think is not active. The SmolLM3 template is not used for this run.
train.evalDatasetNote: The held-out suite is the final gate, never a training or hyperparameter split. Epochs are fixed. Loss is logged. There is no early stopping.

sweep.note: Save an adapter checkpoint every half epoch and gate each one against the held-out suite. A single endpoint cannot distinguish underfitting, overfitting, and a capacity ceiling, because one run is one point and the endpoints lie. Sweeping the whole curve converts that argument into a measurement for the cost of one training run. At 4548 examples and effective batch 32 this is 143 steps per epoch, so checkpoints land every 72 steps.
sweep.readMissesByRegisterNote: This corpus was built to widen register coverage, so the gate report must break misses down by register as well as by class. A per-class-only report cannot tell whether the blunt, crude, imperative, and manipulative registers are now caught, which is the question this run exists to answer.

llamaCpp.note: convert_hf_to_gguf.py then llama-quantize Q8_0. The run records the resolved commit in artifacts.json. Q8_0 matches the live vendor pin's quantization.

time.estimate: Well under two hours on a single 80GB card. 0.6B LoRA, 4548 examples, 3 epochs, sequences around 2k tokens, then per-checkpoint merge, llama.cpp convert, and 187 compact-verdict gate items. If a run is still training after 90 minutes, stop and report: that is a hang, not the expected duration.

publish.when: only after gate-report.json pass is true
publish.note: Publication writes a trainedCandidate on the model manifest. It does not replace the live v2.1 vendor GGUF and it does not change the default evaluator.
